title: Cainite scoundrels
summary: Vampires who live among thieves and charlatans.

claims.text: Many vampires among mortal thieves share their prey’s motives: they rob houses and havens because they can, lacking the skill or chance to play at court.
Some are thugs riding close to the Beast and ruled by greed; others are wretches with no other choice, such as the childe of a disgraced sire or a freed thrall hiding from a vengeful regnant.
Most fall between these extremes, drawn to roguery by both temperament and circumstance.

title: Cainites before Church courts
summary: Vampires caught up in ecclesiastical justice.

claims.text: Cainites who pass as mortals and can claim clerical status may be hauled before an ecclesiastical court for a crime.
A vampire of standing can usually make the problem vanish with bribes and Disciplines, and even a neonate can often manage unless elders work against it.
A real inquest is hard to endure because hearings usually take place by day, and some clergy present hold real faith.

title: The Prometheans
summary: Cainite visionaries of the city underworld.

claims.text: Also known as Firebringers, the Prometheans form a scattered network of dreamers and would-be revolutionaries among urban Cainites.
Their hope is a New Carthage, a fresh pact between vampires and mortals that serves both sides, set against princes, the Silence of the Blood and clan power.
Working among harlots and thieves rather than lords and clergy has kept them largely unnoticed, and they are preparing a revolt without yet launching it.
They are present in most major European cities, among them Paris, London and Venice.

title: The Furores
summary: Young Cainite rebels against their elders.

claims.text: Cainite society favours old over young and strong over weak, and many neonates live as near-slaves to sires and elders, bound by blood oath or debt.
Being the object of an elder’s obsessive affection can be worse than being a servant, since such lovers are often blood bound; and those who know too much are never let go.
Furores are mostly young and live in a very mortal way; few know more of Carthage than the idea of a lost golden age when all Cainites were equal.
All Furores know there have been places where rebels won, and many have seen or taken part in uprisings.

title: The Banu Sasan
summary: The famous rogues of the Islamic world.

claims.text: The Banu Sasan, the Sons of Sasan, are the most remarkable scoundrels of Islamic lands and like to claim descent from Persian royalty.
Islamic vampires use mortal thieves, beggars and tricksters too; skills such as a naqqab’s talent for breaking into underground homes help in raiding enemy havens.

Followers of Set are numerous in Islamic lands and use false-seeming in service of their god, while the Assamites try to curb such crime where they hold sway, their viziers including many legal scholars.
